requirements.R-1:
### R-1 — A zero-dependency Node.js HTTP service starts from `server.js` on `PORT`

**Basis:** S1 (Node.js HTTP server, no npm dependencies), S2 (`server.js`, `PORT`, default 3000).
**Supersedes:** research decision 10's `Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000`, which would accept
`-1`, `70000` and `1.5` as ports; the rule below accepts only an integer in `1..65535` and is the
binding one.
**Preserved/changed:** nothing exists to preserve; this is new.
**Behaviour.** Running `node server.js` from the repository root starts one process that serves
the page and the API over `node:http`. The listening port is `process.env.PORT` when it parses to
an integer in `1..65535`, otherwise `3000`; an unset, empty, non-numeric, zero, negative or
out-of-range value therefore falls back to 3000. Nothing is installed and nothing is built.

**Status after work item 2 (2026-10-27).** All four lines are observed against the built entry
point: `test/server.test.js` spawns `node server.js` on a free port (A-R1.1), reads the startup
line and fetches `/` and `/api/new`, and starts a second process on a taken port for the non-zero
exit and its message (A-R1.4). The document stage's own runs recorded `PORT` unset and `PORT=8081`
binding 3000 and 8081 (A-R1.2), and each invalid value — `abc`, the empty string, `0`, `70000`,
`1.5`, `-1` — printing the 3000 URL (A-R1.3). The service binds `127.0.0.1` only, a posture the
requirements do not name and which AD-15 in `KNOWLEDGE/architecture.md` records; until the
system-test-author stage no case asserted the bound address, and `SYS_LOOPBACK` (2026-10-27) now
does: the process answers on `127.0.0.1` and a connection to the host's non-internal address is
refused.

- **A-R1.1 (positive)** — From a clean checkout with no `node_modules` and no install step,
  `node server.js` starts serving and the process keeps running. Observed at: the terminal and
  any HTTP request. Confirm by: start it on a free port, request `GET /` and `GET /api/new`, then
  stop it; record the startup line and the two status codes.
- **A-R1.2 (boundary)** — With `PORT` unset, the server listens on 3000; with `PORT=8081`, it
  listens on 8081. Observed at: the process's startup log line and the reachable URL. Confirm by:
  start once with `PORT` unset and once with a set port, fetch `/api/new` on each.
- **A-R1.3 (failure)** — An unusable `PORT` (`abc`, the empty string, `0`, `70000`) does not crash
  the server: the documented default (3000) is used. Observed at: the startup log. Confirm by:
  start with each value in turn and fetch the page on 3000.
- **A-R1.4 (failure)** — A port already in use produces a clear error message and a non-zero exit
  instead of a silent hang. Observed at: stderr and the shell exit code. Confirm by: start two
  servers on the same port.
requirements.R-2:
### R-2 — `GET /` serves a playable page titled "Battleship"

**Basis:** S3. **Behaviour.** `GET /` returns a complete HTML document
(`Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`) whose `<title>` is exactly `Battleship`. The response
body already contains the 10×10 grid as 100 `<button class="cell" data-row="R" data-col="C"
aria-label="…">` elements with `R` and `C` in 0–9 — the grid is rendered by the server into the
page shell, not built by client script, so the markup itself is checkable. `data-row="0"`
`data-col="0"` is the top-left cell. Clicking a cell fires at it; the page marks each fired cell as
miss, hit or sunk, shows how many ships remain, announces each outcome in a
`role="status"` region, offers a "New game" control, and disables the grid while a shot is in
flight and after the game ends. When the last ship sinks, the same status region announces the win
in words (that all five ships are sunk) and the "New game" control remains available. All CSS and
JavaScript are inline or served from this repository — no CDN, no build step.

**Status after work item 2 (2026-10-27).** A-R2.1 is observed: the served body has
`<title>Battleship</title>`, exactly 100 row-major cells with `data-row="0" data-col="0"` first, no
off-origin `src`/`href`, and the `role="status"` region and "New game" control the behaviour
names. A document-stage probe then drove the served page once in headless Chrome over the
DevTools Protocol (`RUN/scratch/w2-doc-page-probe.js`): the load announced a ready game with 5
ships, a click on the first square sent its shot, marked it `M` with `aria-disabled="true"` and the
label "Row 1, column 1, miss", wrote "Row 1, column 1: miss. 5 ships remaining." and kept focus on
that square; the walk to the win ended with "All five ships are sunk. You win! Choose New game to
play again.", 67 `M`, 12 `H`, 5 `S` marks, `shipsRemaining` 0 and the grid locked; a click after the
win changed nothing; and "New game" cleared every square, restored 5 and loaded a new id. That is
one observation of A-R2.2, the post-win half of A-R2.3, the click half of A-R2.5 and A-R2.6 — the
named confirmations remain W3's `TC_BROWSER_*` cases and the release's manual consumer check, and
the keyboard path, the accessibility tree and the network-error path (A-R2.4) are not yet
observed.

The verify stage ran a second probe (`RUN/scratch/w2-verify-page-trace.js`) that hands the page's
own handlers answers the real server never sends, and traced two faults it found and fixed: a
200 answer whose body carried no ship count printed `undefined`, and a refused New game had
already cleared the finished game's closed state, so the page offered shots at a game that was
over. Both are A-R2.3/A-R2.4 territory at the page surface: a start is now taken only from an
answer holding an id and an integer ship count, an off-contract shot answer is reported rather
than marked, and a failed start leaves the board exactly as it was — the probe saw the win state
survive a refused New game and a later valid New game still start. A second pass then closed a
race the same probe exposed: New game was live while a shot was in flight, so the shot's answer
could land on a board the player had already replaced. The control is now inert for the duration
of a request (`aria-disabled` plus a guard, so a keyboard user keeps focus), and the probe saw a
click during a slow shot change nothing while that shot landed on the game it belonged to.
`TC_BROWSER_*` (W3) must cover those paths; no suite case can, because W2 ships no browser
facility.

**Status after work item 3 (2026-10-27).** The browser rows are now observed by committed cases
rather than by run-scoped probes. `node --test browser-check/page.js` exits 0 with
`tests 8 / pass 8 / fail 0` over one headless Chrome `156.0.8078.48` and a server per case:
A-R2.2 by `TC_BROWSER_FIRE` (one `POST /api/fire` for one click, the outcome rendered, the count
equal to the answer's `shipsRemaining`, no navigation); A-R2.3 by `TC_BROWSER_LOCK`,
`TC_BROWSER_WIN` and `TC_BROWSER_START_FAIL` (a fired cell sends nothing, `New game` sends no start
while a shot is in flight, the finished board refuses a click on an unfired square, and a board a
failed start left without a game sends nothing either); A-R2.4 by `TC_BROWSER_ERROR` and
`TC_BROWSER_START_FAIL` (a shot that cannot reach the server is reported in the status region,
marks nothing, leaves the count alone, and the retry lands; a failed start is reported and names
`New game` as the way on); A-R2.5 by `TC_BROWSER_KEYBOARD` for its scriptable half (Tab reaches a
cell, a `solid`/`3px` ring, the accessibility name carries the coordinates, Enter fires once and
focus stays, the outcome is text); and A-R2.6 by `TC_BROWSER_WIN` (five `sunk`, twelve `hit`, the
win sentence naming the five ships, the closed board, and a fresh unmarked board from `New game`).
The two paths W2's verify fixed are asserted by the same cases — a refused `New game` leaves the
finished board exactly as it was, and an answer off the contract is reported rather than rendered,
including one whose `gameOver` contradicts its `shipsRemaining`. The screen-reader announcement
and the visual judgement stay the release manual consumer pass (A-R2.5, A-R2.2), which remains
open; the cases are evidence for the same lines, not a substitute for it.

- **A-R2.1 (positive)** — A request for `/` returns 200, a `text/html` content type, and a body
  that contains `<title>Battleship</title>`, carries exactly 100 cell elements (the body matches
  `/data-row="\d" data-col="\d"/g` exactly 100 times, and each of the ten values `data-row="R"`
  appears exactly 10 times), makes `data-row="0" data-col="0"` the first cell in document order,
  and loads nothing from outside this repository (no `src` or `href` value begins with `http://`,
  `https://` or `//`). Observed at: the response body. Confirm by: `test/server.test.js`, which
  fetches `/` and applies those four checks to the returned string (no DOM parser is needed).
- **A-R2.2 (positive)** — Clicking a cell fires exactly one `POST /api/fire` for that cell's
  `data-row`/`data-col` with no navigation or document reload, renders the returned outcome on it,
  and updates the displayed ships-remaining count to the response's `shipsRemaining`. Observed at:
  the browser. Confirm by: the manual consumer check at release (open the page, fire, watch the
  cell change and the count drop on a sink), with `TC_BROWSER_FIRE` covering the same behaviour
  automatically (W3); the request's behaviour is additionally covered at the API layer by R-5's
  tests.
- **A-R2.3 (boundary)** — A cell that has already been fired at cannot be fired again from the
  page (it is not clickable), and the grid does not accept input while a shot is in flight or
  after `gameOver`. Observed at: the browser. Confirm by: `TC_BROWSER_LOCK` and `TC_BROWSER_WIN`
  (W3), plus the manual consumer check.
- **A-R2.4 (failure)** — If a request fails (network error or a non-2xx response), the page shows
  the error in the status region and re-enables the grid rather than appearing to have fired.
  Observed at: the browser, by making the shot's request fail — the browser's own network-error
  path, which `TC_BROWSER_ERROR` injects through CDP `Fetch`, or a non-2xx answer — and watching the
  status region and the grid. Confirm by: `TC_BROWSER_ERROR` (W3), plus the manual consumer check
  (load the page, stop the server, click a cell).
- **A-R2.5 (accessibility, positive)** — Every cell is reachable and fireable by keyboard, keeps a
  visible focus indicator, has an accessible name giving its coordinates, the status region
  announces results without focus moving off the fired cell, and each fired cell's outcome is
  readable as text rather than conveyed by colour alone. Observed at: the browser with a screen
  reader or the accessibility tree. Confirm by: `TC_BROWSER_KEYBOARD` for the focus ring, the
  accessible name, Enter and the focus staying put (W3), plus the manual consumer check (tab to a
  cell, press Enter, hear/see the announcement).
- **A-R2.6 (positive, end state)** — When the last ship sinks, the status region shows a win
  message that names the five-sunk condition, the grid no longer accepts shots, and "New game"
  starts a fresh board whose cells show no previous results. Observed at: the browser. Confirm by:
  `TC_BROWSER_WIN` (W3), plus the manual consumer check (play a game to completion, then start a
  new one).
requirements.R-3:
### R-3 — The computer places a valid, hidden fleet on a 10×10 grid

**Basis:** S1, S3, and research decision 2. **Behaviour.** Each new game places five ships —
carrier 5, battleship 4, cruiser 3, submarine 3, destroyer 2 (17 cells) — at random, axis-aligned,
entirely inside the 10×10 board, with no cell shared by two ships. Ships may touch. Placement is
driven by an injectable random source so it can be reproduced in tests. Each ship is attempted at
most 200 times; if one cannot be placed within that budget, game creation throws an `Error` whose
message names placement, instead of returning a partial fleet.

**Status after work item 1 (2026-10-27).** Implemented and observed at the rules module:
`battleship.js` places the five-ship fleet from an injected random source with the 200-attempt
budget, and its suite exercises composition, 200 seeded placements, seed determinism and the
exhausted-budget throw. **After work item 2 (2026-10-27):** A-R3.5 is now observed too — the
`/api/new` payload carries exactly `game`, `size` and `ships`, every `/api/fire` answer carries
exactly `result`, `gameOver` and `shipsRemaining` through a full walk, and the served page names no
ship cell (`TC_PAGE`, `TC_NEW_GAME`, `TC_WALK`).

- **A-R3.1 (positive)** — A created game has exactly those five ships with those lengths, and
  their cells total 17 distinct coordinates. Observed at: the rules module. Confirm by:
  `test/battleship.test.js`, whose first case asserts the exported `FLEET` constant (5, 4, 3, 3, 2)
  and that the union of ship cells has size 17.
- **A-R3.2 (boundary)** — Every ship cell satisfies `0 <= row <= 9` and `0 <= col <= 9`, each
  ship's cells share a single row or a single column (ships are axis-aligned, never diagonal or
  L-shaped), and no two ships share a cell, over 200 games created from seeds `1..200`. Observed
  at: the rules module. Confirm by: a unit test looping those seeds.
- **A-R3.3 (positive)** — Two games created from the same seed have identical fleets, and seeds
  `1..20` produce more than one distinct fleet. Observed at: the rules module. Confirm by: a
  determinism unit test.
- **A-R3.4 (failure)** — A random source that always returns `0` exhausts the placement budget and
  game creation throws an `Error` whose message names placement, rather than returning overlapping
  ships or hanging. Observed at: the rules module. Confirm by: a unit test that passes such a
  source, asserts the throw and that its message mentions placement, running under an explicit
  per-test timeout (`{ timeout: 5000 }`) — `node:test` applies no default timeout (measured), so
  without one a hang would stall the run instead of failing it.
- **A-R3.5 (information)** — No API response and no page payload ever contains ship positions
  before those cells are fired at. Observed at: the `/api/new` and `/api/fire` response bodies and
  the page source. Confirm by: an API test asserting the new-game payload's exact keys, plus
  inspection of the page source in review.
requirements.R-4:
### R-4 — `GET /api/new` starts a game and returns its id

**Basis:** S4. **Behaviour.** Returns `200` with
`Content-Type: application/json` and the body `{"game": "<uuid>", "size": 10, "ships": 5}`. The id
is a `crypto.randomUUID()` string, unique per call, and identifies that game's state in the
server process.

**Status after work item 2 (2026-10-27).** A-R4.1 and A-R4.2 are observed by `TC_NEW_GAME`: two
consecutive calls return distinct v4 ids, each working with `POST /api/fire`, with a JSON content
type, exactly the three payload keys and no ship or fleet name (C9's pattern). A new game the
rules cannot deal is outside A-R4.1/A-R4.2 and is recorded as AD-17 at the item's verify stage: the
route answers `500 {"error"}` without storing a game, and the process keeps serving
(`TC_ERROR_TABLE (c)`).

- **A-R4.1 (positive)** — Two consecutive calls return two different ids, each an RFC 4122 version
  4 UUID in lower-case hex (`/^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/`),
  and each id works with `POST /api/fire`. Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by: an API test.
- **A-R4.2 (boundary)** — The response carries an `application/json` content type and its payload
  contains exactly `game`, `size` and `ships`; it carries no fleet data. Observed at: the response.
  Confirm by: an API test asserting the content type and the key set.
requirements.R-5:
### R-5 — `POST /api/fire` resolves a shot to `miss`, `hit` or `sunk`

**Basis:** S4, research decision 3. **Behaviour.** Accepts a JSON body
`{"game": "<id>", "row": <int>, "col": <int>}` with `row` and `col` integers in `0..9` (row 0 is
the top row). A shot at an unfired cell of a ship reports `hit`, unless it completes that ship, in
which case it reports `sunk`; a shot at water reports `miss`. A successful response is `200` with
`{"result": "<miss|hit|sunk>", "gameOver": <bool>, "shipsRemaining": <int>}`. A shot at a cell
already fired at, or at a game that is over, is rejected by the rules module without changing its
state; the server turns that rejection into `409` (R-7).

**Status after work item 1 (2026-10-27).** A-R5.4 and A-R5.5 are observed at the rules module: the
repeat-shot refusal leaves the record unchanged and the first shot is the one that counts, and a
seeded game's 17 ship cells resolve 12 `hit` and 5 `sunk` with water reporting `miss`.
**After work item 2 (2026-10-27):** A-R5.1–A-R5.3 are observed at the HTTP API — `TC_WALK` drives
one game row-major to `gameOver` and counts 5 `sunk`, 12 `hit` and a `miss` elsewhere with the
exact three-key body, `TC_COORDINATES` fires the four corners and the values one step outside,
and `TC_REPEAT_FIRE` gets `409` and a game that still reconciles.

- **A-R5.1 (positive, API walk)** — Driving one game to completion through `POST /api/fire` in a
  fixed order — row-major, `row` 0…9 outer and `col` 0…9 inner — and stopping at the first
  response with `gameOver: true` yields exactly five `sunk` responses, twelve `hit` responses and
  a `miss` for every other shot, because the fleet occupies 17 cells of which the last five shots
  fired at them complete ships. Shots after `gameOver` are not part of the walk: R-6.3 refuses them
  with `409`. Every response in the walk has exactly the keys `result`, `gameOver` and
  `shipsRemaining` — no fired-cell list and no ship data — so the walk also confirms R-3.5 at the
  fire endpoint. Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by: `test/server.test.js`, which performs the
  walk against a game created by `GET /api/new` and asserts those counts and key sets.
- **A-R5.2 (boundary)** — `row`/`col` are accepted at both extremes, `0` and `9`, and rejected one
  step outside (`-1`, `10`) with `400`. Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by: an API test.
- **A-R5.3 (failure)** — A repeated shot at an already-fired cell returns `409` with
  `{"error": "..."}` and changes nothing: `shipsRemaining` and later results are unaffected.
  Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by: an API test firing twice at one cell, then completing the
  game and checking the totals still reconcile.
- **A-R5.4 (boundary)** — The first shot at a cell, not the second, is the one that counts: firing
  twice at the same ship cell leaves that ship needing the same number of hits as after one shot.
  Observed at: the rules module. Confirm by: a unit test.
- **A-R5.5 (positive, rules)** — At the rules layer, using a fleet from a seeded game, firing at
  each of the 17 ship cells yields `hit` for the 12 that do not finish a ship and `sunk` for the 5
  that do, and firing at any water cell of the same game yields `miss`. Observed at: the rules
  module. Confirm by: `test/battleship.test.js`.
requirements.R-6:
### R-6 — `gameOver` is true exactly when every ship is sunk

**Basis:** S4. **Behaviour.** Every successful fire response carries a boolean `gameOver`, false
until the shot that sinks the last ship, true from then on. `shipsRemaining` counts ships not yet
sunk.

**Status after work item 1 (2026-10-27).** The rules half of A-R6.1 and A-R6.2 is observed: a game
with one ship afloat after 16 fired ship cells reports not over with one remaining, and the 17th
reports over with none, with the reader of the record agreeing with the field. **After work item 2
(2026-10-27):** the HTTP half is observed too — `TC_WALK` asserts the last response is
`gameOver: true` with `shipsRemaining: 0`, the count falls only on the five `sunk` shots
(5→4→3→2→1→0), and the 16th and 17th ship cells carry the adjacent states; `TC_GAME_OVER_REFUSAL`
gets `409` for shots after the win and a server that keeps serving.

- **A-R6.1 (positive)** — The last response of the A-R5.1 walk has `gameOver: true` and
  `shipsRemaining: 0`, and `shipsRemaining` decreases by one on exactly the five `sunk`
  responses (5 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1 → 0). Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by: the same test.
- **A-R6.2 (boundary)** — In that walk, the response to the 16th ship cell fired at has
  `gameOver: false` and `shipsRemaining: 1`; the 17th ship cell's response has `gameOver: true`
  and `shipsRemaining: 0`. Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by: the same test, asserting both
  adjacent states.
- **A-R6.3 (failure)** — After `gameOver`, a further shot at an unfired cell is refused with `409`
  and does not change the game; `gameOver` stays true. Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by: an
  API test.
requirements.R-7:
### R-7 — Every API failure is a JSON error with a non-2xx status

**Basis:** S4 boundaries; research decision 5. **Behaviour.** `POST /api/fire` answers `400` for a
malformed JSON body, a missing, wrong-type or empty `game`, a non-integer `row`/`col`, or an
out-of-range coordinate; `404` for a non-empty string id the server does not hold; `409` for a fired
cell or a finished game; `413` for a body over 1 MB. A known path reached with the wrong method
(`GET /api/fire`, `POST /api/new`, `POST /`) answers `405`. Paths match exactly after the query
string is stripped, so `/api/new?x=1` is `/api/new` while `/api/fire/` and `/api` are unknown paths
and answer `404` (`/api/fire/` is `404`, not `405`); every other unknown path is `404` too. Every
error body is `{"error": "<message>"}` with a JSON content type. Game ids are opaque handles and are not
validated for format: any non-empty string id the server does not hold is `404`, whether or not it
looks like a UUID; only a missing, non-string or empty `game` is `400`. No request can crash the
process.

**Status after work item 2 (2026-10-27).** A-R7.1–A-R7.3 are observed by `TC_ERROR_TABLE`: the
fourteen-row table answers each documented status with a JSON `{error}` string, `/api/new?x=1` is
`200`, a 1 MB+1 body is `413`, and a valid `GET /api/new` immediately afterwards is `200`. One
`400` row the table above does not name is also observed and recorded as AD-16: a request target
WHATWG `URL` refuses (`GET http://[`) answers `400` and the process keeps serving
(`TC_ERROR_TABLE (b)`). The verify stage traced the other route that reaches the rules module:
`GET /api/new` on a source that cannot place a fleet made `createGame`'s throw end the process, so
that path now answers `500` and keeps serving (AD-17, `TC_ERROR_TABLE (c)`), which is what makes
"No request can crash the process" hold for both routes and not only for `POST /api/fire`.

- **A-R7.1 (positive)** — Each case in this table produces its documented status and a JSON body
  with a non-empty `error` string, except the one 200 case: malformed JSON → 400; `{}` → 400;
  `{"game":id,"row":-1,"col":0}` → 400; `{"game":id,"row":10,"col":0}` → 400;
  `{"game":id,"row":1.5,"col":0}` → 400; `{"game":id,"row":"1","col":0}` → 400;
  `{"game":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000","row":0,"col":0}` → 404;
  `{"game":"not-a-uuid","row":0,"col":0}` → 404; a second shot at a cell already fired at → 409;
  `GET /api/fire` → 405; `POST /api/new` → 405; `GET /api/fire/` → 404; `GET /api` → 404;
  `GET /nope` → 404; `GET /api/new?x=1` → 200; a 1 MB+ body → 413. Observed at: the HTTP API.
  Confirm by: one `test/server.test.js` case walking that table against one live game.
- **A-R7.2 (failure)** — A malformed body, an unknown id, a body over 1 MB, and a wrong-method
  request each leave the server running: a valid `GET /api/new` immediately afterwards returns
  200. Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by: the same test, issuing a valid request after the
  bad ones.
- **A-R7.3 (boundary)** — An unknown path such as `/nope` returns `404` JSON, not the page, and
  every error response carries a JSON content type. Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by: the
  same test.
requirements.R-8:
### R-8 — The game rules live in their own module, separate from HTTP

**Basis:** S5. **Behaviour.** A module at the repository root (`battleship.js`) owns the board
size, the fleet, placement, shot resolution and game-over state. It imports nothing from
`node:http`, knows nothing about requests or responses, and is the only place the rules live;
`server.js` translates HTTP to calls on it and back.

**Status after work item 1 (2026-10-27).** A-R8.1 is observed: the rules suite requires only
`battleship.js` and runs with no server. The module half of A-R8.2 was checked by a source read of
`battleship.js` (no reference to `http`, `req` or `res`, and no `require` at all). **After work item
2 (2026-10-27):** the `server.js` half is observed as well — a source check over the built layer
finds no ship name and no `miss`/`hit`/`sunk` literal in it, and the server reaches the rules only
through `battleship.js`'s exports (step proof C12).

- **A-R8.1 (positive)** — `battleship.js` can be required and exercised in a plain Node process
  with no server running. Observed at: the module's exports. Confirm by: the unit tests, which
  import only the module.
- **A-R8.2 (boundary)** — The module's source contains no reference to `http`, `req`, or `res`,
  and `server.js` contains no fleet data or result strings of its own. Observed at: the two source
  files. Confirm by: a review read of both files at the implement and verify steps.

requirements.R-10:
### R-10 — State ownership and hidden information

**Basis:** interaction and state guidance (`GUIDES/behavioral-requirements.md#actors-channels-and-state-ownership`);
discovery's interaction baseline. **Behaviour.** The server owns the authoritative game state —
fleet, fired cells, game-over — in process memory, keyed by game id, for the lifetime of the
process. The browser owns only the current game id and the rendered view derived from server
responses; it never guesses a result optimistically beyond a pending marker. Ship positions are
never sent to the client. There is no persistence: restarting the process discards every game, and
the page starts a new game on load. No identity, login, sharing or per-user record is introduced.
One process serves every request, and a game's state changes only inside the synchronous call that
applies a shot, after its body is parsed — so two requests for the same cell in flight together
cannot both be accepted: the second observes the cell as already fired and receives `409`.

**Status after work item 2 (2026-10-27).** The server half is observed: the process holds one
`Map` of games and serializes no fleet (`TC_NEW_GAME`, `TC_WALK`, `TC_PAGE`); A-R10.2's two-game
independence and A-R10.5's concurrent double-shot (one `200`, one `409`) are asserted by
`TC_TWO_GAMES` and `TC_CONCURRENT_FIRE`. A-R10.1 and A-R10.3 are browser behaviours and stay
pending W3. **After work item 3 (2026-10-27):** both are observed. `TC_BROWSER_RELOAD` fires once,
reloads, and finds a different id in `document.body.dataset.game`, 100 unmarked cells, the count
back at 5, a recorded `GET /api/new`, and a shot carrying the new id (A-R10.1). `TC_BROWSER_RESTART`
stops the case's server, rebinds the same port, and watches the page's next shot answer `404`, the
status region change, no cell marked and the count unchanged, after which `New game` deals a fresh
board without a page reload (A-R10.3). The page never marks optimistically: a failed shot and an
answer off the contract both leave every cell unmarked.

- **A-R10.1 (positive)** — A page reload starts a fresh game and the earlier game id is no
  longer used by that page. Observed at: the browser. Confirm by: `TC_BROWSER_RELOAD` (W3), plus the
  manual consumer check.
- **A-R10.2 (boundary)** — Two games held at once are independent: firing at a cell in game A never
  changes game B's `shipsRemaining` or its cells. The request shape has no other client, so the
  automated form uses two ids in one process. Observed at: the HTTP API. Confirm by:
  `test/server.test.js`, which creates two games, fires once at cell `(0,0)` of game B, drives game A
  through the A-R5.1 walk to `gameOver`, then asserts that game B still answers a shot at a cell it
  has not had fired at with `200` and `gameOver: false`, and that repeating B's `(0,0)` shot still
  answers `409`.
- **A-R10.3 (failure)** — Restarting the server makes previously issued ids return `404`; the
  page's next shot reports an error and the player can start a new game without reloading being
  required. Observed at: the browser. Confirm by: `TC_BROWSER_RESTART` (W3), plus the manual
  consumer check.
- **A-R10.4 (information)** — Nothing in the page's HTML or JavaScript embeds ship positions, and
  no endpoint returns them; a player cannot read the fleet from the page source before firing.
  Observed at: the page source and API responses. Confirm by: reading the served page in the
  R-2/R-3 tests and review.
- **A-R10.5 (concurrency, boundary)** — Two `POST /api/fire` requests for the same cell, issued
  together with `Promise.all`, produce exactly one `200` and one `409`, and the game's
  `shipsRemaining` afterwards reflects that cell having been fired at once, not twice. Observed at:
  the HTTP API. Confirm by: `test/server.test.js`.
